chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who includes four or five of his freedmen in his Hajj. He said: 'If they are all free men, they receive their reward, but the one who performed Hajj on their behalf does not fulfill the obligatory Hajj for them, and the obligatory Hajj remains for the one who performed it.'

And there is no objection to a woman performing Hajj on behalf of a man if she has already performed her obligatory Hajj and knows the rituals of Hajj. It is not permissible for her to perform Hajj on behalf of another woman if she has not yet performed her own. This is indicated by what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Hajj on behalf of a man or another woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim clarifies the distinction between the obligatory Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam) and supererogatory acts, establishing that while multiple slaves may share the reward of a single Hajj, only the performer fulfills their own mandatory duty. It further specifies the juristic condition that a woman may perform Hajj on behalf of a man due to the permissibility of proxy in his favor, but not for another woman, reflecting the specific legal nuances in Shia fiqh regarding gender and proxy. This highlights the scholarly emphasis on the validity of the performer's prior fulfillment of their own obligation as a prerequisite for valid proxy performance.
